messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — ran a long-context repro for the chat model with AWQ (fp8) and hit repeated GPU OOMs during KV warmup. Suspect kernel selector falling back to fp16 GEMM that allocates huge temp buffers.

katy: Can you paste the kernel_selector / allocator traces?

alex: Pasting the relevant snippets. Note the selector picks matmul_fallback_fp16 for layers 10..12 and workspace_request spikes to ~2.2GB despite quantized weights.

```
[2026-03-17 18:12:01] kernel_selector: layer=10 candidate=matmul_awq_int8 (est_ws=128MB) score=42
[2026-03-17 18:12:01] kernel_selector: layer=10 candidate=matmul_fallback_fp16 (est_ws=2300MB) score=43  <-- chosen
[2026-03-17 18:12:02] allocator: reserve(2.3GB) -> failed, try evict
[2026-03-17 18:12:02] allocator: evicting temp caches, reclaimed 400MB
[2026-03-17 18:12:02] runtime: OOM at workspace allocate 2300MB at layer=10
```

alex: Also KV cache dtype shows "stored_as_uint8" but runtime upcasts to fp16 in the matmul kernel path which forces a scratch copy per head.

ryan: Hmm. Two leads: 1) kernel scoring function prefers fp16 for latency on current HW metrics even when it requires a big scratch; 2) workspace estimate isn't penalized enough in scoring for tight memory regimes.

priya: Could be the batching heuristics too — longer sequences push sequence_len distribution high and batching picks a conservative prefetch window. Any perf profile from the canary run?

alex: Yes, CPU profiler + nvprof snippet below. Notice big stall in memcpy (H2D) right before the OOM.

```
# nvprof summary (truncated)
GPU memcpy H2D: calls=18 total_time=980ms avg=54ms
matmul_fallback_fp16: calls=24 avg_time=8.2ms
matmul_awq_int8: calls=4 avg_time=12.4ms
# timeline: memcpy spikes align with layer 10 allocations
```

katy: That memcpy spike suggests allocation + data movement for upcast buffer. If kernel stayed in int8 path it wouldn't need that. We should adjust kernel_selector scoring to heavily penalize extra workspace when kv_length > X.

ryan: Agreed. Proposed quick fix: add memory_pressure_factor to scoring: score -= ws_bytes / (GPU_mem * 0.8) * 1000. Then we can gate: if kv_cache_bytes + ws_bytes > mem_threshold -> prefer low-ws kernels.

priya: Also think about changing KV cache dtype policy: keep KV in uint8 and implement on-the-fly quantized GEMM kernels that accept uint8 keys to avoid full upcast. That's a larger runtime change though.

alex: For short-term mitigation I tested a config tweak that forces kernel preference order when model_quant == AWQ and kv_dtype==uint8. It reduces OOMs in the sim. Config diff:

```
# runtime config
quant_policy:
  awq:
    prefer_low_workspace: true
kernel_selector:
  memory_pressure_threshold: 0.78
  ws_penalty_scale: 1200
```

alex: After applying, canary run completed with no OOMs, avg latency +6% but much lower tail and no alloc stalls.

katy: Good. Please open a short PR with the config change + unit test for kernel scoring under constrained mem. Tag me and @ryan.

alex: Will do. Also filing a follow-up ticket for a longer-term plan: implement mixed-precision-aware kernels that accept quantized KV and avoid per-batch upcasts; and a profiler hook to instrument "ws_requested" per kernel.

ryan: For the ticket add a perf regression checklist: reproduce with seq=4096, batch=1, awq fp8, kv_len>=2048; baseline (int8-aware kernels) vs current selector. We should also add an alert when allocator starts evicting >500MB in <30s.

alloc-bot: [alert] allocator.evictions.rate high on canary-gpu-03 (window=30s) -> 620MB reclaimed. Link: https://console.internal/redwood/alloc/12345

priya: Nice. One more note — watch FP8 mixed-precision accumulation semantics. Some fp8->fp16 accumulation paths can silently degrade numeric stability leading to soft failures; add a quick eval on a fixed prompt set after forcing selector changes.

alex: Agreed. I'll attach eval results to the PR. Short-term plan: (1) PR kernel scoring tweak (config + test) (2) Canary with monitor for alloc evictions (3) Start design doc for quant-friendly kernel interfaces.

katy: Sounds good. Thanks for the fast triage. :thumbsup:

ryan: If you need help with the profiler hook I can pair tomorrow.

alex: Thanks — pairing would help to spec the event points. I'll ping calendar.
